chunks: Abd al-Samad ibn Muhammad narrated from Hanan ibn Sadir, from his father, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I entered upon Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Hanafiyyah, and his tongue had become paralyzed, so I instructed him to make his will, but he did not respond.

He said: So I ordered a basin, then I put sand in it, and it was placed before him. Then I said to him, 'Write with your hand,' so he wrote his will with his hand in the sand, and I copied it onto a sheet.

key_terms.اعْتُقِلَ لِسَانُهُ: his tongue became impaired or paralyzed, preventing speech
key_terms.الرَّمْلَ: sand used here as a surface for writing
key_terms.الْوَصِيَّةِ: the bequest or final will made before death
key_terms.صَحِيفَةٍ: a sheet or written page onto which the will was copied

ai.seo_question: Can a person who is unable to speak still make a valid will in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith relates an incident in which a dying man who could no longer speak conveyed his will through writing. It indicates the practical validity of expressing a bequest by non-verbal means when speech is no longer possible, which is significant in discussions of wills and end-of-life legal procedure.
